page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is an entry-level general purpose virtual server powered by KVM virtualization. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core across 2 threads on a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor. The compute architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence. Network throughput is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present.

Performance profiles demonstrate polarized capabilities between single-thread and aggregate multi-thread workloads. The server achieves top-quartile single-core benchmark metrics, marked by a stress-ng single-core score of 3070.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1989.0. Conversely, due to its low total core count, multi-core metrics place in the bottom 25%, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 2479.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3814.1. Memory bandwidth is moderate, registering 27.73 GB/sec on large block writes and 38.17 GB/sec on large block reads.

Given its hardware constraints, ecs.g8a.large offers resource-efficient compute for lightweight tasks that prioritize per-core performance over parallel throughput. The instance is suited for microservices, low-traffic web serving, development environments, and lightweight background automation that do not require high concurrency or local disk IOPS.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. Configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core and 8.0 GB of memory, it delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Advanced instruction extensions are present, including AVX-512 and VAES. Benchmark tests demonstrate strong single-core performance reaching the top 25%, while overall multi-core throughput and database operation metrics reflect its small scale, landing in the lower quartiles. This server is best suited for lightweight web application serving, development environments, microservices, and single-thread-dependent background processing tasks.
